answer: Cross-epoch trajectory matching. Each identity’s action history is embedded into a low-dimensional behavioural map; the centroid of its activity must stay within a narrow canyon across epochs. A per-epoch beacon samples random checkpoints, and any identity whose new vertex drifts beyond tolerance is quarantined. To survive, an attacker must run each sybil through the same multi-epoch routine, multiplying operational cost per identity by the number of epochs required to establish consistency.
